analysis.title: back from America: A few quick observations from an intense client trip on the US East Coast this week
key_insights: The market narrative on bonds has reversed from a year ago. Last year the story was that AI is disinflationary and the US Treasury will not allow a bond sell-off. This year the story is that AI issuance is a big driver of higher yields and the Treasury has lost control of the long end.

There were rumors of a coming suspension of 20-year Treasury issuance and a sharp shortening of the maturity of supply. Most clients were still very cautious on fixed income. The author thinks the narrative pendulum has swung somewhat too far the other way.

Client sentiment on France was overwhelmingly bearish, in line with Paul Krugman's commentary overnight. The author disagrees with parallels to 2010-2015, but expects the market to take time to regain confidence after last week's large dislocations.
The French situation is a fresh weight on the EUR that the author did not expect to materialize this year.

The AI discussion with US clients was more nuanced than expected. Data center experts on the author's conference panel raised concerns about slipping underwriting standards, energy supply for construction demand, and whether the expected surge in inference capacity can be met with enough demand and revenue.
A Brookings paper estimates AI labs need to generate close to $4trillion of revenue to earn a return on data center investments.

The author's main client message is that the biggest systemic risk in the market next year is not France but 'something going wrong' in the AI ecosystem, such as a safety event, a failed IPO or disappointing revenues.
The author says concentration risk is immense and that this dollar-negative, bond-positive AI event risk is the most under-priced in markets at the moment.
